title: Libraries Overview
summary: Learn what libraries are and how to include them to save time.

steps.title: What is a Library?
steps.markdownContent:
A **library** is pre-written code that someone else created to make your life easier.

Instead of writing 500 lines of complex math to talk to a temperature sensor, you can use a library that reduces it to one line: `sensor.readTemp();`.

Libraries exist so engineers don't have to reinvent the wheel for every common component!

steps.title: How to Use a Library (#include)
steps.markdownContent:
To use a library, you add an `#include` line at the very top of your sketch, before `setup()`.

```cpp
#include <Servo.h>
```

This tells the compiler to attach the Servo motor code to your sketch before compiling. If you try to command a servo without including the library, the compiler will fail and give you an error.

steps.title: Arduino Library Manager
steps.markdownContent:
Where do libraries come from? 

The Arduino IDE has a built-in **Library Manager** (under Tools > Manage Libraries). It's like an app store for code! You can search for the sensor or motor you are using, and click Install. Use the simulator below to find and install a library.
